transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Aurum Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Aurum Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Aurum CISO)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, we've got about 45 minutes, want to make sure we map your SLA and incident tolerances for inference across hosted / dedicated / private. quick intros?

[00:18] Lena: hi lena here, i run the ML platform at Aurum, we're rolling out conversational product recs and want predictability at p99.

[00:26] Marcus: Marcus, platform, i care about routing, multi-region, and how we failover without double billing.

[00:32] Priya: priya, CISO, quick on security and audit requirements - we need KMS and HSM, SSO with SAML, and SOC2 alignment.

[00:40] Samira: great, daniel and i will cover ops patterns and tradeoffs. Daniel, want to kick into fallback story?

[00:46] Daniel: sure. So high level, Redwood supports three deployment modes -- Hosted API for fast start, Dedicated pools for reserved GPUs, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full control. For outages we expose routing policies: region-first, cost-preferred, and canary fallback chains. The typical pattern we see is primary region -> cross-region fallback -> cheaper model variant fallback -> degraded partial responses.

[01:12] Marcus: can you explain "model variant fallback"? i want to avoid inconsistent outputs across regions.

[01:18] Daniel: yes. Model variant fallback means if the primary model isn't available we route to a compatible version or smaller quantized variant. outputs can vary but we provide model-family mapping and automated reranking to keep quality consistent. there's also request tagging so you can track which model served the request.

[01:36] Lena: what's the control plane for that? does the routing happen at DNS level or a proxy? we run internal infra behind a WAF so we prefer not to open a public endpoint.

[01:46] Daniel: good question. In Hosted, routing is managed by Redwood's control plane and our edge proxies; requests hit an edge in-region and we do smart routing. For Dedicated you can opt for a customer VPC peering or private link; routing still honors your policies but happens inside your network boundaries. For Private we hand over the control plane and you manage routing, but we provide the same policy templates.

[02:10] Priya: on data residency, does log/audit content ever leave region? audit logs must stay in EMEA for certain customers.

[02:18] Samira: we can pin logs and telemetry retention by region for Dedicated/Private; Hosted can be configured but has constraints. we support KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and HSM options for Private. we'll share the security doc.

[02:30] Marcus: latency SLOs — we've seen p99 jumps during cold starts; what's Redwood's approach to cold start and KV cache warmup?

[02:38] Daniel: runtime uses continuous batching + KV cache prewarming for recent prefixes. cold-starts can be mitigated with pinned warm replicas on Dedicated. for Hosted we have burst capacity but it's probabilistic. rough numbers we've seen: p50 in single-digit ms for embeddings, p99 dependent on sequence length and model, e.g. 600-900ms for larger models unless you pin.

[03:02] Lena: our SLO target is p99 < 450ms for the shopping recs path (95% of traffic is short seqs, 5% long). can Redwood meet that on Hosted?

[03:12] Daniel: on Hosted probably not consistently for large models; if you pick a smaller model family or Dedicated with pinned GPUs we can tune. Also quantization helps - we can recommend int8/int4 profiles depending on quality budget.

[03:26] Marcus: if we go Dedicated and have multi-region pools, how does failover affect billing? we don't want to be charged double for active capacity in both regions.

[03:34] Daniel: Dedicated uses reserved capacity, you pay for committed capacity per pool. for active failover you can either run cold standby in another region (lower cost) or autoscale burst when needed. Redwood can also support a 'warm-replica' low-cost instance for faster failover. We can model cost scenarios for you.

[03:58] Priya: incident scenarios - what's the RTO and RPO for the control plane? we've got compliance auditors who will ask.

[04:06] Samira: SLAs differ by product. Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Hosted has best-effort with published performance profiles. RTO for control plane failover is typically minutes, data plane (inference) failover depends on network and warm replicas. we'll share the SLA matrix.

[04:30] Lena: can we do canary rollouts of a new model across a percentage of traffic and automatically rollback if error budget is crossed?

[04:38] Daniel: yes - the console supports canary ramping, automatic rollback triggers based on latency/error thresholds, and canary to different model variants. you can also run percentage-based routing per feature flag.

[04:52] Marcus: what about debugging during incidents — is there trace-level visibility? we need token-level latency breakdowns.

[04:58] Daniel: Redwood Console includes per-request tracing hooks, token-level latency, and KV cache hit metrics. we can stream traces into your datadog/splunk via connectors. some fields are PII so you'd control retention.

[05:18] Priya: security again — SSO, RBAC, audit trail retention. we need immutable audit logs for 1 year. can that be exported to our S3?

[05:26] Samira: yes for Dedicated/Private you can set retention and export audit logs to your S3. Hosted supports shorter retention in default plan but can be extended as an add-on.

[05:36] Lena: do you support model-level drift/regression alerts? if a fallback model produces worse recommendations we need QA gate.

[05:44] Daniel: Redwood Optimize ties evals to rollouts. you can attach prompt sets and quality metrics and block a rollout if quality drops beyond a threshold. we'll share an example eval harness.

[05:58] Marcus: edge case: region A goes down, region B takes traffic but has a different model variant - how do we reconcile customer experience differences?

[06:06] Daniel: recommended approach: keep family mapping consistent across regions; prefer same architecture family, only fall back to smaller variant as last resort. also annotate responses with model version so you can measure UX drift. For strict consistency, use Private with synchronized model artifacts.

[06:28] Lena: any limitations on model pinning across nodes? like can we force a particular commit hash?

[06:34] Daniel: yes, you can pin model versions in Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports version pinning but with some rollout constraints.

[06:44] Samira: let's talk incident playbooks. Typically customers want: degraded mode (limited features), partial responses, and notification windows. Do you have required SLAs for different features?

[06:56] Lena: we want a spec: if p99 > 1.5s for 3 minutes trigger fallback to smaller model + alert. also want a 30-min incident notification SLA.

[07:08] Marcus: and automatic throttling so UI doesn't cascade retries — we want token backpressure.

[07:14] Daniel: we have per-route rate limiting, adaptive throttling, and token-level budget controls. can gate retries with jitter.

[07:24] Priya: on certifications: SOC2 and ISO are mandatory for our vendor list. do you have those?

[07:30] Samira: Redwood is SOC 2 type 2 and pursuing ISO. for Dedicated/Private we'll provide relevant audit artifacts; for Hosted we have standard attestation.

[07:40] Lena: what's the onboarding timeline for a Dedicated pilot? we need to scope capacity and do a bench.

[07:46] Daniel: typical pilot takes 3-4 weeks: scoping, traffic profile import, benchmark run, canary, then expand. We'll propose a pilot run with sample traffic and tail-latency benchmarks.

[07:58] Marcus: about benchmarks — can you run them inside our cloud account? we want realistic network conditions.

[08:04] Daniel: yes, for Dedicated we can run in your VPC via private link, run tail-latency tests, and produce the p50/p95/p99 distributions. we'll need your test harness or we can provide client load generator.

[08:18] Lena: ok i want specifics: show me an incident chain example where the primary CPU OOMs and we need to fail over without losing in-flight responses.

[08:28] Daniel: in that case we recommend: 1) request-level retries with idempotency keys, 2) store streaming partials to your staging cache (or Redwood's prefix cache), 3) automated re-route to warm replica, 4) a post-incident reconciliation job. if you need strict exactly-once semantics we can design with Kafka-like acknowledgements but latency increases.

[08:54] Priya: about keys - if we use customer-managed KMS, can Redwood access plaintext model inputs for debug? we need to restrict access.

[09:02] Samira: with CMK we can do envelope encryption; Redwood engineers do not have plaintext access by default. access for debug is audited and requires approval. in Private deployments you fully control keys.

[09:16] Marcus: competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and Vertex's managed endpoints. how do you compare on predictable p99 and region failover?

[09:24] Daniel: Anthropic is great for model quality but less flexible on private deployments; Vertex is tightly integrated with cloud infra but you manage more of the ops. Redwood aims for a middle ground: production-focused primitives (rollback, tracing, batching) and multiple deployment modes. EdgeServe is a smaller inference vendor we talked about - more ops-heavy.

[09:44] Lena: cost sensitivity — we need ballpark numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted for our traffic.

[09:50] Samira: we'll send a cost model. quick rule: Dedicated is more predictable unit cost; Hosted is pay-as-you-go but spikes can increase unit cost. Also caching and batching reduce per-token cost; Optimize gives recommendations.

[10:04] Marcus: what telemetry do we need to feed you to run your cost/perf optimizer?

[10:08] Daniel: token-level latency samples, request size distribution, and sequence length histograms. a week of production traces is ideal.

[10:18] Lena: ok we'll provide that after this call.

[10:22] Samira: let's go through a quick timeline if you choose Dedicated pilot: Day 0-3 scoping and infra, Day 4-10 model deploy + bench, Week 3 canary run, Week 4 expand. Does that align with your org's timelines?

[10:36] Lena: yes, we want pilot complete before peak season in mid-august.

[10:42] Priya: one more question — legal: can we get a data processing addendum and standard security terms?

[10:48] Samira: yes we'll include DPA and standard security appendix. we can sign a mutual NDA if necessary.

[11:00] Marcus: any gotchas we should be aware of?

[11:04] Daniel: watch out for model drift when fallbacking models — ensure evals and QA gates are in place; also cross-region egress costs if you do multi-region active-active.

[11:18] Lena: tradeoff noted.

[11:22] Samira: recap and next steps: we'll send Dedicated pricing + SLA matrix and canary docs by Friday (2026-07-10). Daniel will share tail-latency benchmark plan and template. Lena to share traffic percentiles and a short list of critical endpoints. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-07-20.

[11:42] Priya: thanks all, appreciate detail.

[11:46] Lena: thanks, bye.

[11:48] Samira: bye.
